from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Optional

from temporalio import workflow

from banking_workflows.shared_objects import (
    DepositResponse,
    TransferInput,
    TransferOutput,
    TransferStatus,
)

with workflow.unsafe.imports_passed_through():
    from banking_workflows.activities import AccountTransferActivities

TASK_QUEUE = "MoneyTransfer"


@workflow.defn
class AccountTransferWorkflow:

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.progress = 0
        self.transferState = ""
        self.depositResponse = DepositResponse("")
        self.start_to_close_timeout = timedelta(seconds=5)
        self.retry_policy = AccountTransferActivities.retry_policy

    @workflow.run
    async def transfer(self, input: TransferInput) -> TransferOutput:
        workflow_type = workflow.info().workflow_type
        logger = workflow.logger
        logger.info(f"Simple workflow started {workflow_type}, input = {input}")
        idempotencyKey = str(workflow.uuid4())

        # Validate
        await workflow.execute_activity(
            AccountTransferActivities.validate,
            args=[input],
            start_to_close_timeout=self.start_to_close_timeout,
            retry_policy=self.retry_policy,
        )
        await self.updateProgress(25, 1)

        # Withdraw
        await workflow.execute_activity(
            AccountTransferActivities.withdraw,
            args=[idempotencyKey, input.amount, workflow_type],
            start_to_close_timeout=self.start_to_close_timeout,
            retry_policy=self.retry_policy,
        )
        await self.updateProgress(50, 3)

        # Deposit
        self.depositResponse = await workflow.execute_activity(
            AccountTransferActivities.deposit,
            args=[idempotencyKey, input.amount, workflow_type],
            start_to_close_timeout=self.start_to_close_timeout,
            retry_policy=self.retry_policy,
        )
        await self.updateProgress(75, 1)

        # Send Notification
        await workflow.execute_activity(
            AccountTransferActivities.sendNotification,
            args=[input],
            start_to_close_timeout=self.start_to_close_timeout,
            retry_policy=self.retry_policy,
        )
        await self.updateProgress(100, 1, "finished")

        return TransferOutput(DepositResponse(self.depositResponse.get_chargeId()))

    @workflow.query(name="transferStatus")
    def queryTransferStatus(self) -> TransferStatus:
        workflow.logger.info("Workflow has been queried")
        return TransferStatus(
            self.progress, self.transferState, "", self.depositResponse, 0
        )

    async def updateProgress(
        self, progress: int, sleep: int, transferState: Optional[str] = "running"
    ) -> None:
        if sleep > 0:
            await asyncio.sleep(sleep)

        self.transferState = transferState
        self.progress = progress

import asyncio
from datetime import timedelta

from temporalio import workflow
from temporalio.common import RetryPolicy

with workflow.unsafe.imports_passed_through():
    from activities import (
        extract,
        get_available_task_queue,
        load,
        poll,
        transform,
        validate,
    )
    from dataobjects import DataPipelineParams


@workflow.defn
class DataPipelineWorkflowHappyPath:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._progress = 0

    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, input: DataPipelineParams) -> str:
        workflow_type = workflow.info().workflow_type
        workflow.logger.info(f"The data pipeline for {input} beginning.")

        workflow.logger.info("Searching for available worker")
        unique_worker_task_queue = await workflow.execute_activity(
            activity=get_available_task_queue,
            start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=10),
        )
        workflow.logger.info(f"Matching workflow to worker {unique_worker_task_queue}")

        # Set progress to 10%
        self._progress = 10

        # Sleep 2 seconds
        await asyncio.sleep(2)

        validation = await workflow.execute_activity(
            validate,
            input,
            start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=300),
            heartbeat_timeout=timedelta(seconds=20),
        )
        if validation is False:
            workflow.logger.info(f"Validation rejected for: {input.input_filename}")
            return "invalidated"

        # Set progress to 20%
        self._progress = 20

        activity_output = await workflow.execute_activity(
            extract,
            input,
            task_queue=unique_worker_task_queue,
            start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=300),
            heartbeat_timeout=timedelta(seconds=20),
        )
        workflow.logger.info(f"Extract status: {input.input_filename}: {activity_output}")

        # Set progress to 40%
        self._progress = 40

        activity_output = await workflow.execute_activity(
            transform,
            input,
            task_queue=unique_worker_task_queue,
            start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=300),
            heartbeat_timeout=timedelta(seconds=20),
        )
        workflow.logger.info(f"Transform status: {input.input_filename}: {activity_output}")

        # Set progress to 60%
        self._progress = 60

        activity_output = await workflow.execute_activity(
            load,
            input,
            task_queue=unique_worker_task_queue,
            start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=300),
            heartbeat_timeout=timedelta(seconds=20),
        )
        workflow.logger.info(f"Load status: {input.input_filename}: {activity_output}")

        # Set progress to 80%
        self._progress = 80

        activity_output = await workflow.execute_activity(
            poll,
            args=[input, workflow_type],
            task_queue=unique_worker_task_queue,
            start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=3000),
            heartbeat_timeout=timedelta(seconds=20),
            retry_policy=RetryPolicy(initial_interval=timedelta(seconds=2), backoff_coefficient=1),
        )

        workflow.logger.info(f"Poll status: {input.input_filename}: {activity_output}")

        # Set progress to 100%
        self._progress = 100

        return f"Successfully processed: {input.input_filename}!"

    @workflow.query
    def progress(self) -> int:
        return self._progress

"""LoanUnderwritingWorkflow — Temporal + Strands + HITL.

Flow:
  1. TemporalAgent assesses the application using credit_check and
     calculate_debt_to_income tools.
  2. Workflow pauses and exposes the AI assessment via a query so the
     starter can display it to the booth visitor.
  3. Visitor sends an approve() or reject() signal.
  4. Workflow completes with the final LoanDecision.
"""

import os
from datetime import timedelta
from typing import Optional

from temporalio import workflow
from temporalio.contrib.strands import TemporalAgent
from temporalio.contrib.strands.workflow import activity_as_tool
from temporalio.common import RetryPolicy, VersioningBehavior

with workflow.unsafe.imports_passed_through():
    from prompts import UNDERWRITING_SYSTEM_PROMPT
    from shared import LoanApplicant, LoanDecision
    from tools import calculate_debt_to_income, credit_check

_versioning_kwargs = (
    {"versioning_behavior": VersioningBehavior.PINNED}
    if os.environ.get("TEMPORAL_ENV") == "cloud"
    else {}
)


@workflow.defn(**_versioning_kwargs)
class LoanUnderwritingWorkflow:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.agent = TemporalAgent(
            name="LoanUnderwritingAgent",
            start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=60),
            tools=[
                activity_as_tool(
                credit_check,
                start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=30),
                retry_policy=RetryPolicy(
                    initial_interval=timedelta(seconds=2),
                    maximum_attempts=4,
                ),
            ),
                activity_as_tool(calculate_debt_to_income, start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=30)),
            ],
            system_prompt=UNDERWRITING_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
        )
        self._assessment: Optional[str] = None
        self._human_decision: Optional[str] = None
        self._final_decision: Optional[LoanDecision] = None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Signals
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @workflow.signal
    def approve(self) -> None:
        self._human_decision = "APPROVED"

    @workflow.signal
    def reject(self) -> None:
        self._human_decision = "REJECTED"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Queries
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @workflow.query
    def get_assessment(self) -> Optional[str]:
        """Returns the AI assessment once complete, or None if still running."""
        return self._assessment

    @workflow.query
    def get_final_decision(self) -> Optional[LoanDecision]:
        """Returns the final LoanDecision once the human has decided, or None if still waiting."""
        return self._final_decision

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Run
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, applicant: LoanApplicant) -> LoanDecision:
        prompt = (
            f"Please assess the following loan application:\n\n"
            f"Applicant Name: {applicant.name}\n"
            f"Applicant ID: {applicant.id}\n"
            f"Occupation: {applicant.occupation}\n"
            f"Annual Income: ${applicant.annual_income:,.2f}\n"
            f"Loan Amount Requested: ${applicant.loan_amount:,.2f}\n"
            f"Loan Purpose: {applicant.loan_purpose}\n"
            f"Additional Context: {applicant.fun_fact}\n"
        )

        result = await self.agent.invoke_async(prompt)
        self._assessment = str(result)

        # Parse AI recommendation out of the structured response
        ai_recommendation = "REJECT"  # safe default
        for line in self._assessment.splitlines():
            if line.strip().startswith("RECOMMENDATION:"):
                value = line.split(":", 1)[-1].strip().upper()
                if "APPROVE" in value:
                    ai_recommendation = "APPROVE"
                break

        # Wait for the human underwriter (booth visitor) to decide
        await workflow.wait_condition(lambda: self._human_decision is not None)

        human_override = self._human_decision != (
            "APPROVED" if ai_recommendation == "APPROVE" else "REJECTED"
        )

        self._final_decision = LoanDecision(
            applicant_name=applicant.name,
            ai_recommendation=ai_recommendation,
            ai_reasoning=self._assessment,
            human_decision=self._human_decision,
            human_override=human_override,
        )

        return self._final_decision

"""Ziggy dynamic agent: each turn runs a caller-supplied Python script (no model in the loop).

A deliberately minimal harness agent. Each turn carries an arbitrary Python *script* (see
:class:`RunScript`) that runs in a sandbox whose only escape hatches are the travel host
functions — each backed by a durable Temporal activity. There is no model in the loop: the
"plan" arrives pre-written as the script.

It's a thin consumer of the harness Code Mode feature: :func:`agent.code_mode_tool` turns the
travel activity tools into a single run-a-script tool, and the ``run_script`` handler dispatches
the caller's script straight through it. The script calls the tools as async host functions;
each host call runs as a durable, approval-gated activity, and independent calls can run
concurrently via ``asyncio.gather``.

Contrast with the conversational Ziggy agent (``conversational_workflow.py``): that one drives
the Gemini Interactions API with a model in the loop, over the same Code Mode tool. This one has
no model — the script is the input. Both reuse the standard harness contract: ``@agent.defn`` +
an :class:`AgentWorkflowRunner` built in ``@agent.init``, the turn loop driven by the ``run``
that ``@agent.defn`` generates, and a single ``@agent.accepts`` handler (``run_script``) whose return
value becomes the turn's reply.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from temporalio import workflow
from temporalio.contrib.workflow_streams import WorkflowStream

with workflow.unsafe.imports_passed_through():
    from temporal_agent_harness.harness import agent
    from temporal_agent_harness.harness.agent_protocol import (
        AgentConfig,
        MidTurn,
        TextReply,
        ToolApprovalPolicy,
    )
    from temporal_agent_harness.harness.agent_workflow import AgentWorkflowRunner

    from . import activities, choices, trip_board
    from .models import RunScript


@agent.defn(name="ZiggyDynamicAgent")
class ZiggyDynamicAgentWorkflow:
    # There is no model in this agent, so the script is what keeps the board current; see
    # `trip_board.py`.
    trip_board = agent.state(trip_board.TripBoard)

    @agent.init
    def __init__(self, config: AgentConfig) -> None:
        self._runner = AgentWorkflowRunner(
            config,
            stream=WorkflowStream(),
            # The travel tools run inside a sandboxed simulation (no real-world side effects),
            # so this agent skips approvals by default. A caller can still tighten this per
            # session via AgentConfig.approval_policy.
            approval_policy_default=ToolApprovalPolicy.dangerously_skip_all(),
        )
        # Code Mode over the travel tools plus the board tools: one tool that runs a script
        # calling them all as host functions. The run_script handler dispatches the caller's
        # script straight through it.
        self._run_code = agent.code_mode_tool(
            [*activities.ALL_TOOLS, *trip_board.BOARD_TOOLS, *choices.CHOICE_TOOLS],
            name="run_travel_code",
            # Supplied per host call and hidden from the script: a script names a trip, never
            # the state the board lives in.
            injections={"board": self.trip_board},
        )

    # ENQUEUE: a parent drives this one turn at a time through the subagent FIFO gate, but a
    # human can also address this agent directly at the same time — so a second message should
    # wait its turn rather than be rejected.
    @agent.accepts(mid_turn=MidTurn.ENQUEUE)
    async def run_script(self, message: RunScript) -> TextReply:
        r"""Execute a Python ``script`` in a sandbox over the travel host functions, returning its
        printed output + final value.

        The sandbox has no filesystem, network, or arbitrary imports — only ``asyncio`` plus the
        host functions below, each backed by a durable Temporal activity. Everything else is
        ordinary in-sandbox Python. The value of the script's LAST EXPRESSION becomes the reply
        (alongside anything ``print``ed), so end the script with the value you want back.

        The host functions are ``async`` — you MUST ``await`` them — so structure the script as::

            import asyncio
            async def main():
                ...                 # await host functions here
                return <final value>
            asyncio.run(main())

        Run INDEPENDENT host calls concurrently with ``asyncio.gather`` (a gathered batch runs
        concurrently, each call its own durable activity); only await sequentially when a later
        call needs an earlier call's result. Each host function takes ONE argument — a dict
        matching its request shape — and returns a dict; index results with normal Python
        (``resp["flights"][0]["price_usd"]``). Scripts are statically type-checked against these
        signatures before running, so a wrong argument shape or an unknown result key comes back
        as an error to fix rather than a result (a bad script is normal input, not a failure).

        Host functions (all ``async``, all must be awaited):

          • ``search_flights({"origin": str, "destination": str, "date": str}) -> dict``
                Returns ``{"flights": [flight, ...]}``, each flight: ``flight_id``, ``airline``,
                ``departure_time`` ("HH:MM"), ``arrival_time`` ("HH:MM"), ``price_usd`` (float,
                the economy fare), ``stops`` (int), and ``fares``: one per ``level``
                ("economy" | "premium" | "business"), each with ``price_usd`` and ``changeable``.
          • ``get_seat_map({"flight_id": str}) -> dict``
                Returns ``{"flight_id": str, "open_seats": [seat, ...]}``, each seat: ``seat``
                ("14C"), ``cabin`` (a fare level), ``extra_usd`` (exit rows cost extra), and
                ``features``: what the seat is like, drawbacks included ("window", "exit row",
                "extra legroom", "no under-seat storage", "limited recline", ...).
          • ``search_hotels({"city": str, "check_in": str, "check_out": str}) -> dict``
                Returns ``{"hotels": [hotel, ...]}``, each hotel: ``hotel_id``, ``name``,
                ``star_rating`` (int), ``price_per_night_usd`` (float), ``neighborhood`` (str).
          • ``book_flight({"flight_id": str, "passenger_name": str, "fare": str}) -> dict``
                ``fare`` defaults to "economy". Returns ``confirmation_code``, ``flight_id``,
                ``passenger_name``, ``fare``, ``price_usd``, ``status``.
          • ``select_seat({"confirmation_code": str, "flight_id": str, "passenger_name": str,
            "fare": str, "seat": str}) -> dict``
                Chooses an open seat in the fare's cabin on a booked flight; pass the booking's
                details as ``book_flight`` returned them. Returns ``confirmation_code``, ``seat``,
                ``features``, ``extra_usd``, ``status``.
          • ``book_hotel({"hotel_id": str, "guest_name": str}) -> dict``
                Returns ``confirmation_code``, ``hotel_id``, ``guest_name``, ``status``.

        The remaining host functions keep the agent's **trip board** — its running TODO list of
        the trips it is collecting, which is observable state: every call publishes JSON Patch
        ops on the turn stream, so a watching client sees the board change as the script runs.
        Open a trip before searching, and record each booking as it happens rather than at the
        end. All take one dict and return one dict (``read_trip_board`` takes nothing and
        returns a string); every board response carries ``trip_id``, ``status``, ``remaining``,
        ``note`` and a rendered ``board``.

          • ``open_trip({"description": str, "traveler": str, "tasks": [str, ...]}) -> dict``
                Puts a trip on the board and returns its ``trip_id``. ``tasks`` is the starting
                checklist; omit or leave empty for the standard one.
          • ``record_booking({"trip_id": str, "kind": "flight"|"hotel", "confirmation_code": str,
            "detail": str, "price_usd": float, "fare": str, "completes": [str, ...]}) -> dict``
                Records a booking and ticks off the checklist items it finishes, in one commit.
                Use a confirmation code a booking call actually returned.
          • ``record_seat({"trip_id": str, "confirmation_code": str, "seat": str}) -> dict``
                Records the seat ``select_seat`` gave a recorded flight.
          • ``complete_trip_tasks({"trip_id": str, "tasks": [str, ...]}) -> dict``
                Ticks items off by their text (exact, or a distinctive part of it).
          • ``add_trip_tasks({"trip_id": str, "tasks": [str, ...]}) -> dict``
                Adds items the trip turned out to need.
          • ``set_trip_status({"trip_id": str, "status": "collecting"|"booked"|"cancelled"}) -> dict``
          • ``read_trip_board() -> str``
                The whole board, rendered. Takes no arguments.

        ``trip_id`` accepts ``"latest"`` for the most recently opened trip.

        Example — open the board, search concurrently, book, record, summarize::

            import asyncio
            async def main():
                trip = await open_trip({
                    "description": "SFO to JFK, Jul 1-5",
                    "traveler": "Ada Lovelace",
                })
                flights, hotels = await asyncio.gather(
                    search_flights({"origin": "SFO", "destination": "JFK", "date": "2026-07-01"}),
                    search_hotels({"city": "New York", "check_in": "2026-07-01", "check_out": "2026-07-05"}),
                )
                cheapest = min(flights["flights"], key=lambda f: f["price_usd"])
                flight = await book_flight({
                    "flight_id": cheapest["flight_id"],
                    "passenger_name": "Ada Lovelace",
                    "fare": "economy",
                })
                await record_booking({
                    "trip_id": trip["trip_id"],
                    "kind": "flight",
                    "confirmation_code": flight["confirmation_code"],
                    "detail": f"{cheapest['airline']} {cheapest['flight_id']} "
                              f"{cheapest['departure_time']}-{cheapest['arrival_time']}",
                    "price_usd": flight["price_usd"],
                    "fare": flight["fare"],
                    "completes": ["outbound flight"],
                })

                aisle = [s for s in seats["open_seats"] if s["cabin"] == "economy" and "aisle" in s["features"]]

agentic-sdlc.code:
"""IssueToProduction: an issue labeled for the agents becomes a reviewed, deployed change.

Agents decide what to do inside a step. This Workflow decides the process: which agent works
when, what a person must approve, how people's comments reach the agents, what to retry, when to
stop spending, and how to undo a bad release. Read ``run`` top to bottom; it is the whole
lifecycle.

People drive it entirely from GitHub. The planner asks its questions on the issue and people
reply there; a comment while coders work steers them; comments on the PR are feedback (fixed on
the spot) or a scope change (the run goes back to planning); a comment once the change is on
staging gets it adjusted there. Only people with write access are heard. The three promotions,
the plan, the merge (when supervised) and production, are not comments: the run starts a release
workflow in the storefront repo whose job waits on a GitHub Environment with required reviewers,
and a reviewer approves or rejects the deployment in GitHub's UI. That is where the permission to
promote lives. The console only shows what's happening.

Every agent is a child Workflow (agents/workflows.py) whose model calls and tool calls are
Activities, so a crashed worker, a rate-limited provider or a two-hour wait for a person loses
no work.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from datetime import timedelta

from temporalio import workflow
from temporalio.exceptions import ApplicationError

with workflow.unsafe.imports_passed_through():
    from agentic_sdlc import config
    from agentic_sdlc.activities.checks import CheckActivities
    from agentic_sdlc.activities.deploy import CheckInput, CheckResult, DeployActivities, DeployCall
    from agentic_sdlc.activities.github import (
        CODER,
        PLANNER,
        BranchesInput,
        BranchRef,
        ClosePrInput,
        GitHubActivities,
        MergeInput,
        MergePrInput,
        PrepareRunInput,
        PullRequest,
        PullRequestInput,
        RevertInput,
        ReviewInput,
        RunRepo,
    )
    from agentic_sdlc.models import (
        ClarifyReply,
        CodeReply,
        CodeRequest,
        Command,
        Feedback,
        Plan,
        PlanReply,
        PlanRequest,
        ReviewReply,
        ReviewRequest,
        RunRequest,
        RunState,
        Step,
        Subtask,
        Workspace,
    )
    from agentic_sdlc.pipeline.base import GITHUB, MAX_TEST_FIX_ROUNDS, QUICK, AgentRun, _count, _duration
    from agentic_sdlc.pipeline.environments import DeployRequest

# Each Worker Deployment Version starts with one PIPELINE_VERSION and never changes it, so a
# Pinned run always replays against the code path it started on. v2 adds a security-review
# agent. In a real project v2 would simply be the next commit; see README "Notes".
SECURITY_REVIEW = config.PIPELINE_VERSION == "v2"

MAX_PLAN_ROUNDS = 3
MAX_PLAN_REVISIONS = 3  # scope changes that send the run back to planning
MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS = 5  # rounds of PR feedback before the run gives up
MAX_STAGING_ROUNDS = 5  # adjustments made on staging before the agents ask for a new issue
CANARY_WEIGHT = 20


@workflow.defn
class IssueToProduction(AgentRun):
    @workflow.init
    def __init__(self, request: RunRequest) -> None:
        self._begin(request, _initial_steps())
        self._staging_rounds = 0

    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, request: RunRequest) -> RunState:
        self._publish()
        try:
            repo = await self._take_issue()
            answers = await self._clarify(repo)
            new_requirements: list[str] = []
            while True:
                plan = await self._plan(repo, answers, new_requirements)
                branches = await self._build(repo, plan)
                pr = await self._open_pull_request(repo, plan, branches)
                await self._review(repo, plan, pr)
                scope_change = await self._review_window(repo, plan, pr)
                if scope_change is None:
                    break
                new_requirements.append(scope_change.text)
                await self._start_over(repo, pr, scope_change)
            merge_sha = await self._merge(repo, pr)
            await self._deploy_to_staging(merge_sha)
            release = await self._ask_to_ship(repo, plan)
            if release.name == "/stop":
                await self._stop(repo, release.argument)
                return self._state
            shipped = await self._canary(repo, self._state.staging_sha or merge_sha)
            await self._finish(repo, shipped)
        except ApplicationError as err:
            self._state.status = "failed"
            self._note_failure(str(err))
            raise
        finally:
            self._finish_steps()
            await self._close_agents()
        return self._state

    # -- Steps -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def _take_issue(self) -> RunRepo:
        async with self._step("issue"):
            repo = await workflow.execute_activity_method(GitHubActivities.prepare_run, PrepareRunInput(
                repo=self._request.repo, issue_number=self._request.issue_number, branch_prefix=self._branches,
            ), **GITHUB)
            self._home = repo.issue_number
            self._track(issue=repo.issue_number)
            self._state.issue_url = repo.issue_url
            self._detail("issue", f"Issue #{repo.issue_number}")
            return repo

    async def _clarify(self, repo: RunRepo) -> str | None:
        """The planner asks about anything the issue leaves open; people reply on the issue,
        and the answers go into the plan."""
        planner = await self._planner(Workspace(repo=repo.repo, branch=repo.base_branch))
        async with self._step("clarify"):
            reply = await self._turn(planner, "clarify", self._plan_request(), ClarifyReply)
            questions = reply.clarification.questions[:3]
            if not questions:
                self._detail("clarify", "Nothing to ask: the issue is clear enough to plan")
                self._skip("gate:clarify", "The planner had no questions")
                return None
            self._detail("clarify", f"{_count(len(questions), 'question')} for the developer")
            await self._post(repo.issue_number, _questions_comment(questions), agent=PLANNER)
        outcome = await self._wait_for_people(
            "clarify", "The planner asked its questions on the issue", questions=questions,
            commands=["/skip"], issue=repo.issue_number, github_url=repo.issue_url)
        for item in outcome.comments:
            item.kind = "answer"
            self._resolve(item, "addressed", "Used in the plan")
        return "\n".join(c.text for c in outcome.comments) or None

    async def _plan(self, repo: RunRepo, answers: str | None, new_requirements: list[str]) -> Plan:
        planner = await self._planner(Workspace(repo=repo.repo, branch=repo.base_branch))
        feedback: str | None = None
        if new_requirements:
            feedback = "Requirements added during review:\n" + "\n".join(f"- {r}" for r in new_requirements)
        for _round in range(MAX_PLAN_ROUNDS):
            async with self._step("plan"):
                reply = await self._turn(planner, "plan", self._plan_request(answers, feedback), PlanReply)
                plan = reply.plan
                plan.subtasks = plan.subtasks[:3]
                self._state.plan = plan
                self._detail("plan", f"{len(plan.subtasks)} subtask(s): " + ", ".join(s.title for s in plan.subtasks))
                await self._post(repo.issue_number, _plan_comment(plan, self._state.plan_revision, repo.repo),
                                 agent=PLANNER, labels=["agent-plan"])
            ask = await self._request_release("plan", f"issue:{repo.issue_number}", repo.base_branch)
            outcome = await self._wait_for_people(
                "plan", "The plan is on the issue, waiting for a reviewer to approve it on GitHub", plan.summary,
                issue=repo.issue_number, github_url=_release_url(repo.repo), release=("plan", ask))
            if outcome.decision:
                if not outcome.decision.approved:
                    raise ApplicationError(
                        f"The plan was rejected by @{outcome.decision.reviewer}: {outcome.decision.comment or 'no reason given'}",
                        non_retryable=True)
                return plan

"""Flight Deck workflows.

FlightSessionWorkflow: the game is a workflow. The browser streams telemetry
to it every second (so a crashed/reloaded tab resumes from workflow state),
and every game action in that batch (collision, repair tap, blaster shot,
kill, Temporal deploy...) becomes its own activity. Gameplay never waits on
them: the Update returns immediately and the activities run in the background.

LeaderboardWorkflow: a long-running entity workflow holding the top 10.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
from datetime import timedelta

from temporalio import workflow
from temporalio.common import RetryPolicy
from temporalio.exceptions import ActivityError, ApplicationError

with workflow.unsafe.imports_passed_through():
    from ..shared.leads import Lead, save_lead
    from .activities import GAME_ACTIVITIES, submit_score
    from .days import day_key, day_label
    from .names import callsign, display_name
    from .models import (
        MAX_EVENTS_PER_BATCH,
        MAX_POINTS_PER_SEC,
        SCORE_SLACK,
        FinishResult,
        LeaderboardEntry,
        LeaderboardInput,
        LeaderboardView,
        ActivityReceipt,
        ActivitySummary,
        DayPodium,
        GameEvent,
        SessionInput,
        SessionState,
        SubmitResult,
        Telemetry,
    )

TOP_N = 10
EVENT_LOG_MAX = 40
# How long to keep an unfinished session (e.g. the visitor walked away) open.
ABANDON_AFTER = timedelta(minutes=10)
EVENT_TYPES = set(GAME_ACTIVITIES) | {"sector"}
GAME_ACTIVITY_RETRY = RetryPolicy(
    initial_interval=timedelta(milliseconds=200), backoff_coefficient=2, maximum_interval=timedelta(seconds=2), maximum_attempts=6
)


@workflow.defn
class FlightSessionWorkflow:
    @workflow.init
    def __init__(self, inp: SessionInput) -> None:
        # Init from input here (not in run) so updates that arrive in the
        # first workflow task already see the state.
        self.s = SessionState(session_id=inp.session_id, station=inp.station, game_ms=inp.game_ms)
        self.s.name = display_name(inp.email, inp.session_id)
        self.counts: dict[str, int] = {}
        self.retries: dict[str, int] = {}
        self.failed = 0
        self.pending = 0

    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, inp: SessionInput) -> SessionState:
        # The lead is captured at launch, so it's saved even if the visitor
        # walks away mid-game. Telemetry keeps flowing while this runs.
        if inp.email:
            await workflow.execute_activity(
                save_lead,
                Lead(
                    id=str(workflow.uuid4()),
                    email=inp.email,
                    demo="flight",
                    station=inp.station,
                    consent_text_version=inp.consent_text_version,
                    captured_at=workflow.now().isoformat(),
                    extra=json.dumps({"name": self.s.name, "session_id": inp.session_id}),
                ),
                start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=10),
            )
        try:
            await workflow.wait_condition(lambda: self._state.status == "finished", timeout=ABANDON_AFTER)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            self._state.status = "abandoned"
        # Let in-flight game activities land before the workflow closes.
        await workflow.wait_condition(lambda: self.pending == 0 and workflow.all_handlers_finished())
        return self._view()

    def _schedule(self, ev: GameEvent) -> None:
        """Start one activity for a game event, without blocking the Update."""
        fn = GAME_ACTIVITIES.get(ev.type)
        if fn is None:
            return
        self.pending += 1
        asyncio.create_task(self._run_game_activity(fn, ev))

    async def _run_game_activity(self, fn, ev: GameEvent) -> None:
        try:
            r: ActivityReceipt = await workflow.execute_activity(
                fn, ev, start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=5), retry_policy=GAME_ACTIVITY_RETRY
            )
            self.counts[ev.type] = self.counts.get(ev.type, 0) + 1
            if r.attempt > 1:
                self.retries[ev.type] = self.retries.get(ev.type, 0) + r.attempt - 1
        except ActivityError:
            self.failed += 1
        finally:
            self.pending -= 1

    @property
    def _state(self) -> SessionState:
        return self.s

    # ---- telemetry ----
    @workflow.update
    def telemetry(self, t: Telemetry) -> SessionState:
        s = self._state
        if t.seq <= s.seq:  # duplicate/late batch (client retry): ignore
            return self._view()
        s.seq = t.seq
        s.elapsed_ms = min(t.elapsed_ms, s.game_ms)
        s.score = t.score
        s.distance = t.distance
        s.hull = t.hull
        s.broken = list(t.broken)
        s.durable = t.durable
        s.deploys = t.deploys
        s.repairs = t.repairs
        s.damage_taken = t.damage_taken
        s.temporal_charges = t.temporal_charges
        s.next_threshold = t.next_threshold
        s.event_log = (s.event_log + [f"{e.t_ms // 1000:>2}s {e.type}{':' + e.kind if e.kind else ''}" for e in t.events])[-EVENT_LOG_MAX:]
        for ev in t.events:
            self._schedule(ev)
        if s.elapsed_ms >= s.game_ms:
            s.status = "ended"
        return self._view()

    @telemetry.validator
    def _validate_telemetry(self, t: Telemetry) -> None:
        s = self._state
        if s.status not in ("playing",):
            raise ApplicationError(f"game is {s.status}", non_retryable=True)
        if t.seq <= s.seq:
            return
        if len(t.events) > MAX_EVENTS_PER_BATCH:
            raise ApplicationError(f"too many events in one batch ({len(t.events)})", non_retryable=True)
        bad = {e.type for e in t.events} - EVENT_TYPES
        if bad:
            raise ApplicationError(f"unknown event types: {sorted(bad)}", non_retryable=True)
        if t.elapsed_ms < s.elapsed_ms:
            raise ApplicationError("time went backwards", non_retryable=True)
        if t.score < s.score:
            raise ApplicationError("score can only go up", non_retryable=True)
        dt = (t.elapsed_ms - s.elapsed_ms) / 1000
        if t.score - s.score > MAX_POINTS_PER_SEC * dt + SCORE_SLACK:
            raise ApplicationError(
                f"impossible score jump: +{t.score - s.score} in {dt:.1f}s", non_retryable=True
            )

    # ---- finish ----
    @workflow.update
    async def finish(self) -> FinishResult:
        """Post the final score to the booth leaderboard (name was set at launch)."""
        s = self._state
        s.status = "finished"
        res: SubmitResult = await workflow.execute_activity(
            submit_score,
            LeaderboardEntry(
                session_id=s.session_id,
                name=s.name or callsign(s.session_id),
                score=s.score,
                station=s.station,
                deploys=s.deploys,
                at=workflow.now().isoformat(),

photo-booth.code:
"""PhotoBoothWorkflow: photo + email in, AI photo strip out, emailed to the visitor.

The booth can reset as soon as the workflow is started (or even just spooled
locally, see spool.py). From then on Temporal owns the job: AI calls retry
until they succeed, across worker restarts and network outages, and the
visitor gets the email whenever it finishes.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import timedelta

from temporalio import workflow
from temporalio.common import RetryPolicy
from temporalio.exceptions import ActivityError, ApplicationError

with workflow.unsafe.imports_passed_through():
    from ..shared.email import EmailMessage, send_email
    from ..shared.leads import Lead, save_lead
    from .activities import (
        CONTENT_POLICY,
        AnalyzeInput,
        ComposeInput,
        PlaceholderInput,
        RenderResult,
        RenderSceneInput,
        analyze_photo,
        compose_strip,
        make_animated_strip,
        render_placeholder,
        render_scene,
    )
    from .analysis import PhotoAnalysis
    from .scenes import BY_ID, FALLBACK, pick_four

# AI calls: retry forever (capped backoff) within a day. A booth outage or a
# flaky model delays the email; it never loses the photo.
AI_RETRY = RetryPolicy(
    initial_interval=timedelta(seconds=2),
    backoff_coefficient=2.0,
    maximum_interval=timedelta(seconds=60),
    maximum_attempts=0,  # unlimited
    non_retryable_error_types=[CONTENT_POLICY],
)
AI_TIMEOUTS = dict(
    schedule_to_close_timeout=timedelta(hours=24),
    start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(minutes=3),  # one image edit; slow ones take ~1 min
    heartbeat_timeout=timedelta(seconds=30),
)
PLUMBING_RETRY = RetryPolicy(initial_interval=timedelta(seconds=2), maximum_interval=timedelta(seconds=60),
                             maximum_attempts=0)


@dataclass
class PhotoBoothInput:
    session_id: str
    station: str
    photo_path: str  # relative to media_dir
    email: str
    consent_text_version: str = ""
    provider: str = "mock"  # fixed at capture time so a session never mixes providers
    analysis_provider: str = "heuristic"  # openai whenever a key exists, even with mock images
    style: str = "inspired"  # prompt style, fixed at capture time
    public_base_url: str = "http://localhost:8000"  # for links in the email
    captured_at: str = ""  # ISO timestamp from the booth (may be long before the workflow starts)


@dataclass
class StepState:
    key: str
    label: str
    state: str = "pending"  # pending | running | retrying | done | failed | skipped
    attempts: int = 0
    detail: str = ""
    url: str | None = None
    seconds: float = 0.0


@dataclass
class PhotoBoothStatus:
    session_id: str
    stage: str = "starting"  # processing | sending | done
    steps: list[StepState] = field(default_factory=list)
    photo_url: str | None = None
    strip_url: str | None = None
    animated_url: str | None = None
    email: str | None = None
    provider: str = ""
    analysis: PhotoAnalysis | None = None


def _is_policy_refusal(err: ActivityError) -> bool:
    return isinstance(err.cause, ApplicationError) and err.cause.type == CONTENT_POLICY


@workflow.defn
class PhotoBoothWorkflow:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._s: PhotoBoothStatus | None = None

    def _step(self, key: str) -> StepState:
        assert self._s
        return next(s for s in self._s.steps if s.key == key)

    @workflow.query
    def status(self) -> PhotoBoothStatus:
        return self._s or PhotoBoothStatus(session_id="")

    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, inp: PhotoBoothInput) -> PhotoBoothStatus:
        session_dir = inp.photo_path.rsplit("/", 1)[0]
        scene_ids = pick_four(workflow.random())
        s = self._s = PhotoBoothStatus(
            session_id=inp.session_id,
            stage="processing",
            photo_url=f"/media/{inp.photo_path}",
            email=inp.email,
            provider=inp.provider,
            steps=[StepState("scan", "Scanning your photo")]
            + [StepState(f"render-{i}", f"Frame {i + 1}: {BY_ID[sid].title}") for i, sid in enumerate(scene_ids)]
            + [StepState("strip", "Developing photo strip"), StepState("animate", "Animating strip"),
               StepState("email", "Beaming strip to your inbox")],
        )

        # Lead first: it's the one thing we must never lose.
        await workflow.execute_activity(
            save_lead,
            Lead(email=inp.email, demo="holodeck-photobooth", station=inp.station,
                 consent_text_version=inp.consent_text_version,
                 id=str(workflow.uuid4()), captured_at=inp.captured_at or workflow.now().isoformat(),
                 extra=json.dumps({"session_id": inp.session_id, "scenes": scene_ids, "provider": inp.provider})),
            start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=15), retry_policy=PLUMBING_RETRY)

        # 1. Analyse the photo: framing, face boxes, usable? Drives prompts and crops.
        scan = self._step("scan")
        scan.state = "running"
        a = await workflow.execute_activity(
            analyze_photo, AnalyzeInput(inp.photo_path, inp.analysis_provider),
            activity_id="scan", retry_policy=AI_RETRY, **AI_TIMEOUTS)
        s.analysis = a
        scan.state = "done"
        who = f"{a.face_count} people" if a.face_count > 1 else a.framing.replace("_", " ")
        scan.detail = who if a.usable else f"{a.reason or 'hard to see you'}: improvising"

        # 2. Four frames in parallel. A content-policy refusal gets one softer
        # prompt, then a bland fallback scene, then a branded placeholder card.
        async def render(i: int, scene_id: str) -> str:
            st = self._step(f"render-{i}")
            st.state = "running"
            tries = [(scene_id, False, ""), (scene_id, True, "-soft"), (FALLBACK.id, True, "-fallback")]
            res: RenderResult | None = None
            for sid, soft, suffix in tries:
                try:
                    res = await workflow.execute_activity(
                        render_scene,
                        RenderSceneInput(session_dir, i, sid, inp.photo_path, inp.provider, a, soft, inp.style),
                        activity_id=f"render-{i}{suffix}", retry_policy=AI_RETRY, **AI_TIMEOUTS)
                    if suffix:
                        st.detail = "softened prompt" if suffix == "-soft" else f"swapped to {FALLBACK.title}"
                    break
                except ActivityError as e:
                    if not _is_policy_refusal(e):
                        raise
                    workflow.logger.warning("frame %s refused by content policy (%s)", i, sid)
            if res is None:
                res = await workflow.execute_activity(
                    render_placeholder, PlaceholderInput(session_dir, i, BY_ID[scene_id].title),
                    start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=30), retry_policy=PLUMBING_RETRY)
                st.detail = "provider refused every prompt"
            st.state, st.url, st.attempts, st.seconds = "done", res.url, res.attempt, res.seconds
            if res.attempt > 1 and not st.detail:
                st.detail = f"done after {res.attempt} attempts"
            return res.path

        frames = await asyncio.gather(*(render(i, sid) for i, sid in enumerate(scene_ids)))

        # 3. Compose the strip, then the animated version.
